name: Papaya
perishability: Perishable once ripe (2–4 days). Picked at colour break, it travels about a week.
summary: A fast crop that fruits within a year of planting and then all year round, so supply is steady and prices stay in a narrower band than most fruit. Papaya ringspot virus and waterlogging are the main risks; a single heavy monsoon spell can kill a field in two days.

key_numbers.label: World rank
key_numbers.note: India grows roughly 40% of world papaya

global: India is the world's largest papaya producer; exports of fresh fruit are small (Gulf, Nepal), while papain (dried latex) is exported for the food and pharma industries.

states.basis: Major producing states (ranked approximately; shares not shown)

seasons.name: Monsoon planting
seasons.note: Bears from about March onwards for 2–3 years.

seasons.name: Autumn planting
seasons.note: Avoids the monsoon at the seedling stage.

seasons.name: Spring planting
seasons.note: Common where frost or waterlogging are risks.

lean_season: No true lean season; supply dips after heavy monsoons and cold winters in the North.

climate.v: 22–35 °C ideal; growth slows below ~12 °C; frost kills plants.
Regular irrigation; standing water for 24–48 hours kills plants.
Shallow roots and a single stem make plants topple in storms.

weather_risks.impact: Collar rot and plant death within days.
Leaf burn, poor fruit set, bland fruit.
Flower drop and sunburn on fruit.

pests.name: Papaya ringspot virus (PRSV)
pests.impact: The main constraint; mottled leaves and ringed fruit, orchards decline within a year.

pests.name: Papaya mealybug
pests.impact: Invasive since 2008; controlled largely by released parasitoids.

postharvest.storage: 10–13 °C, 85–90% RH for fruit at colour break.
postharvest.chilling: Chilling injury below ~10 °C (uneven ripening, hard lumps).
practices: Harvested when the first yellow streaks show; each fruit wrapped in paper or foam net.
Shipped in crates or trucks padded with straw; bruising is the main loss.
Raw papaya is sold as a vegetable; green fruit is tapped for papain latex.

steps.what: Weekly harvests; traders buy at the farm gate by weight.
Ripened at wholesale or retail; sold per kg or per piece.

supply_chain.packaging: Crates or loose with straw; individually wrapped fruit.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Coorg Honey Dew, Washington, CO series

trade.exports: Small fresh exports to the Gulf and Nepal; papain exports.

policy.what: Classical biocontrol (parasitoid release) brought the invasive papaya mealybug under control.

history.what: Papaya mealybug invasion damaged orchards in Tamil Nadu and the South.
Waterlogging kills fields in Gujarat and AP.

signals: Monsoon rainfall and waterlogging in AP, Gujarat and MP.
business: Steady year-round supply makes papaya a reliable staple for fruit bowls and cut-fruit businesses.
Cut papaya and ready-to-eat cups carry large mark-ups.
Short orchard life (2–3 years) means area responds quickly to prices.
